Q: Count only qualifying rows per group from a JOINED table using Codeigniter A:

Simply add your filtering logic to the LEFT JOIN condition logic. This way only qualifying related rows will be counted.

public function getCatsWithItemCounts(): array
{
    return $this->db
        ->select('c.name, COUNT(i.id) count')
        ->join(
            'items',
            'c.id = i.category_id AND i.active = 1',
            'left'
        )
        ->group_by('c.name')
        ->get('categories c')
        ->result();
}

Q: Best way set up protected Route in react using JWT? A:

Basically refresh a token each 13 mins with setTimeout, because 15 is too late. Set a 13 min timeout after login. Estimate timeout length based on exp date if there's a token but no timeout yet (a page was refreshed within 15 min window). Better use 1 min intervals instead of a single timeout to check against supposed exp date because of the way browsers throttle background tabs, add additional check on tab focus.

There's no need to allow authenticated user to access login page. You can decode a token to check exp date on client side for auth-related logic, but user's time can be wrong or token refresh may fail, so server auth always has priority. A token is discarded after any 401 response. Depending on your case, it may be helpful to have api endpoint to confirm auth state (e.g. get user profile) on client side navigation. Otherwise this may result in worse UX: a user successfully navigates to a page that has done no api requests yet, starts working with it, api request occurs and responds with 401, a user is redirected to login

Q: How can I shorten this border checking code? A:

First, you don't need to use elif statements when simple if statements suffice:

    if dx == -1 and self.x == 0:
        return False
    if dx == 1 and self.x == w.return_width() - 1:
        return False
   ... # etc.

I am working on the assumption that you are either moving horizontally or vertically, but not both at the same time (that is, dx and dy cannot both be non-zero). If my assumption is correct, then you are doing more checks then you need to. For example, let's say dx == -1 but self.x != 0. In this case you execute the next elif statement testing dx == 1, which cannot be True. Your code can now be simplified to:

def border_check(self, w, dx, dy):
    if dx == -1:
        return self.x != 0

    if dx == 1:
        return self.x != w.return_width() - 1

    if dy == -1:
        return self.y != 0

    # Must be that dy == 1
    return self.y != w.return_height() - 1

If my assumption is False, and both dx and dy can be non-zero, then:

def border_check(self, w, dx, dy):
    at_border = (
        dx == -1 and self.x == 0
        or
        dx == 1 and self.x == w.return_width() - 1
        or
        dy == -1 and self.y == 0
        or
        dy == 1 and self.y == w.return_height() - 1
    )
    
    return not at_border

Q: How to list installed packages on Google Container Optimized OS? A:

The Container-Optimized OS from Google comes with CoreOS Toolbox located under /usr/bin/toolbox. This toolbox provides apt as package manager. The following should therefore give you a list of installed packages:

$ toolbox apt --installed list

Q: Codeigniter count number of articles in one category while listing categories A:

For your code to work you need two changes:

  • First you join type should be a "left join". Than way you still will get a count result (0) even if a category has no videos yet.
  • Second you need to group your results to be able to use the aggregate function count().

Try with this:

$this->db
->select('categories.c_name, COUNT(videos.id) as num_videos')
->from('categories')
->join('videos', 'categories.c_name = videos.v_category', 'left')
->group_by('categories.c_name');

Also you should reconsider your DB design. If you have id columns in both tables (wich I assume are the primary key) then you should define the relationship between the tables (foreign keys) using the id column, not the name.
